reference.question: A line passes through \((0,-1)\) and has slope \(-2\). What is \(y\) when \(x=3\)?
reference.solution:
Method 1: Write and evaluate the point-slope equation

\(y+1=-2(x-0)\). When \(x=3\), \(y=-1-6=-7\).
